3. SAMPLING

3.1 Lot-

In any consignment all the material belonging manufacture shall be formed into a lot. Each lot separately for judging the conformity to the specification.

to one batch of shall be tested

3.2 Sampling from Bulk - When the supply of cellulose acetate flakes is made in bulk, one lot shall be formed for every 5 tonnes or part Samples of material from each lot shall be collected at regular thereof. intervals when the material is unloaded. The gross sample collected from each lot shall be not less than 5 kg.

7. DETERMINATION

7.0 Outline of the Method-The finely divided cellulose acetate is allowed to stand in contact with a mixture of acetone and sodium hydroxide solution. The amount of alkali consumed for hydrolyzing the material is fo:ntd out by titration. 7.1 Reagents 7.1.1 Sodium Ifwlroside sYolution7.1.2 7.1.3 7.1.4 Stdj)hwic Aciddcelone carbon X. dioxide-free, approximately N.

approximately ( m/m ).

95 percent

Phenolphthalein -

6'5 percent

solution

(al/v ) in alcohol.

7.2 Procedure-Weigh accurately about 2 g of the finely powdered and dried material into a 250-ml stoppered conical flask. Shake the test portion evenly over the base of the flask and, withollt lifting the flask from the work-bench, carefully run in 80 ml of acetone and slake for one hour. Add with continual stirring 50 ml of sodium hydroxide and continue shaking for 3 hours. Wash down the stoppes with water, adding about 50 ml of water to the contents of the flask. Add exactly 50 ml of sulphuric acid and about 0'5 ml of phenolphthalein indicator. Allow to stand for 30 minutes with occasional shaking. Titrate the excess acid against standard sodium hydroxide. Conduct a blank determination on the reagents used. 6

8.3 Procedure - Select an appropriate U-tube viscometer and clean it by rinsing with suitable solvents, followed by ethyl ether. Remove each solvent by passing a current of dry air through it and take care that no moisture remains inside the instrument. Suspend the cleaned viscometer in the bath maintained at 25 i 0*5"C, taking care that the capillary Weigh to the nearest 1 mg, 6 g of the dried material arm is vertical. Stopper into a 250-ml stoppered bottle containing 100 ml of acetone. the bottle and shake in a linear shaker till the solution is complete. Fill the viscometer with the solution using a long pipette to minimize any wetting of the tube along the filling mark. Allow the viscometer to reach the test temperature and adjust the volume to bring the liquid to After the sample has reached the within 2 mm of the filling mark. t&t temperature, apply suction or pressure to bring the liquid level up to Release the suction of` a point at least 1 cm above the timing mark. pressure and measure the time required for the bottom of the meniscus to pass from the top edges of time marks. 7

OF CLARITY

9.1 ProcedurePour a 6 percent (m/u) solution of the material prepared as described in 8.3, slowly through the sides into a clarity tube made of glass, having an outer diameter of 1.4 cm and wall thickness of 1 mm, closed at one end and graduated in centimetres and having a black spot of 4 mm diameter at the flat base end, taking care to avoid air bubbles. Stop pouring the liquid at the point the black spot at the base becomes just invisible when viewed through the liquid column vertically against normal day light. Measure this height of liquid column and report as clarity. 10. DETERMINATION 10.1 Procedure -Fill OF HEAT STABILITY

a heat-resistant glass tube 150 mm long, 12'5 mm diameter and 1 mm wall thickness to about 50 mm with the material. Place the test tube in a bath of glycerine or other suitable mineral oil so that half of the column vf the sample is above the level of the liquid in the bath. Heat the bath at a uniform rate. When the temperature has reached 18O"C, the rate of heating shoulcl be regulated to about 2�C per minute. Ob serve the colour of the sample in the tube. The temperature at which cellulose acetate changes colour to brown is recorded. The heating is continued and the temperature at which the sample fuses is also recorded.
